content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills can be inconsistent without clear structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through design, scaffolding, validation, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md structure and optional resource folders.
Guides planning from user examples into reusable scripts, references, and assets.
Provides init_skill.py to scaffold a starter skill folder with placeholders.
Provides quick_validate.py to check frontmatter, naming, and description rules.
Provides package_skill.py to validate and create a .skill archive.
Includes reference guides for workflow structure and output patterns.
limitations: The scaffold contains placeholders that authors must replace or delete.
Validation is basic and does not replace a full security review.
Scripts write local files and should run only in intended directories.
It does not supply domain expertise for every new skill idea.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Plan the skill purpose, choose resource folders, scaffold the project, and replace placeholders with focused guidance.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review SKILL.md, split long guidance into references, and align bundled resources with real user workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Skill Package
use_cases.description: Run validation, fix frontmatter and naming issues, then create a distributable .skill archive.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new skill idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a new skill for [task]. Ask only the most important questions, then propose the SKILL.md structure and resource folders.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these example user requests, identify which scripts, references, and assets this skill should include. Keep SKILL.md concise.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold and Validate
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation after the design is clear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a skill named [name] in [path]. Then list which placeholder files I should edit or delete.

prompt_templates.title: Review for Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Check SKILL.md, bundled resources, validation results, packaging readiness, and marketplace risks.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for recurring API release notes.
output: A concise skill purpose and trigger description.
A proposed SKILL.md outline for the release note workflow.
Recommended reference files for API style rules and changelog examples.

output_examples.input: Validate and package an existing skill.
output_examples.output: A validation summary, a list of blocking metadata issues, and a packaging status with the generated archive location.

output_examples.input: Improve a complex skill with too much content in SKILL.md.
output_examples.output: A leaner SKILL.md plan, reference file split suggestions, and guidance for when each reference should be loaded.

best_practices: Start from concrete user examples before writing the skill body.
Keep SKILL.md focused and move detailed material into references.
Validate scripts and packaging before sharing the skill.
anti_patterns: Leaving generated placeholder files in the final skill.
Putting broad background material in SKILL.md when a reference file is better.
Packaging a skill before checking frontmatter, naming, and resource relevance.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete skill automatically?
faq.answer: It can scaffold a starter folder, but the author must replace placeholders with domain-specific guidance.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is portable for AI agents that support skill-style workflows and resources.

faq.question: What files does it generate?
faq.answer: The initializer creates SKILL.md plus example scripts, references, and assets folders.

faq.question: Does validation check security issues?
faq.answer: No. The validator checks basic structure, frontmatter, naming, and description constraints.

faq.question: When should I add a script to a skill?
faq.answer: Add a script when a task needs deterministic behavior or repeated code that should not be rewritten each time.

faq.question: When should I use reference files?
faq.answer: Use references for detailed guidance that is only needed for specific tasks or variants.
